Rome fell in 476, yet nine countries on this map have laid claim to its legacy. Who claimed what, and when.

a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ Germany and Austria: Charlemagne was crowned Roman emperor in 800, and Otto I revived the title in 962. The Holy Roman Empire then lasted over eight centuries. Even the word Kaiser comes from Caesar.
2/ Bulgaria: Simeon I (893-927) took the imperial title and dreamed of capturing Constantinople. Around 924-926 Pope John X recognised him as Emperor of the Romans.
3/ Serbia: Stefan Dušan was crowned emperor at Skopje on 16 April 1346, as emperor of the Serbs and Romans. Historians think he aimed to take Constantinople.
4/ Turkey and Greece: the Byzantines called themselves Romans to the end. After taking Constantinople in 1453, the Ottomans later traced their state's lineage back through Byzantium to Rome.

5/ Russia: the monk Philotheus wrote that two Romes had fallen, the third stood, and there would be no fourth. Ivan III married Sophia Palaiologina, a niece of the last Byzantine emperor, and Ivan IV was crowned tsar in 1547.
6/ France and Italy: Napoleon crowned himself in 1804 with a replica of Charlemagne's crown and called his son King of Rome. Mussolini proclaimed an Italian Empire in 1936 after conquering Ethiopia.
Which claim was the strongest? Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
